I'll pull your intents and recent payments, plus run the built-in analysis.
**Short answer:** the actual spending is fine — 1.28 USDC spent against 67 USDC authorized. The problems are in how the intents are *configured*, not what was bought. Overall risk: **medium**.

## What was actually spent (last 30 days)
| Intent | Purpose | Spent | Cap | Used |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0x4e0866` | Cloud infra autopay | 0.98 | 2 | 49% |
| `0xe88b02` | Marketing trial (Revoked) | 0.20 | 5 | 4% |
| `0xb530e9` | Research/datasets | 0.10 | 50 | 0.2% |
| `0x568222` | General ops (discretionary) | 0.00 | 10 | 0% |

All 4 payments have receipts, none exceeded a per-tx cap, and every intent that actually transacted is pinned to a single merchant. That part is clean.

## Three things worth your attention

**1. Open-ended discretionary intent (highest risk)**
`0x568222` is Active with **no merchant allowlist at all** and a 10 USDC cap — yet it has made zero payments in 30 days. There's no usage history justifying an unrestricted allowlist. Pin it to specific merchants, or revoke it since it's never been used.

**2. Possible duplicate or split charge on cloud infra**
Two identical **0.49 USDC** payments hit merchant `0x1111…` **7 seconds apart**, each at 98% of the 0.5 per-tx cap. That's either a ~0.98 invoice being split into two txs to slip under the cap, or a duplicate/retry. Worth checking directly — if it's a split, your per-tx cap is defeating its own purpose and should be sized to the real invoice (~1.0–1.2). Note it also burned 49% of a *weekly* intent's total cap on day one.

**3. Oversized authorization on research intent**
`0xb530e9` authorizes 50 USDC against 0.10 spent. Dropping to ~5 USDC still leaves 50x headroom and removes 45 USDC of standing exposure — the single biggest risk reduction available.

**Also:** the revoked marketing intent `0xe88b02` has **0.8 USDC stranded**. Call `withdrawRemainder` to reclaim it.

## One caveat on the data
All four payments landed within a **64-second span on 2026-09-13**, despite the 30-day window. So there's no real spending history here — this looks like a freshly set-up or test wallet. Any conclusion about burn rate or "correct" cap sizing rests on a single day of activity, and the two 0.49 charges can't be confirmed as duplicate vs. split without the receipt contents. Treat the cap recommendations as directional until you have a few weeks of real usage.

data.headline: Spending itself is tiny (1.28 USDC against 67 USDC authorised, 1.9% utilisation), but two structural problems need attention: an unrestricted-merchant discretionary intent with a 10 USDC cap and zero usage, and a cloud-infra intent where two identical 0.49 USDC charges landed 7 seconds apart at 98% of the per-tx cap.

findings.title: Authorisation vastly exceeds observed spend
findings.detail: Across 4 intents, 67 USDC is authorised while only 1.28 USDC has been spent in the 30-day window. The gap is concentrated in 0xb530e9 (50 USDC cap, 0.1 USDC spent, 0.2% used) and 0x568222 (10 USDC cap, 0 spent). Standing authorisation of this size is exposure without a matching demonstrated need.

findings.title: Unrestricted merchant allowlist on the discretionary ops intent
findings.detail: 0x568222 ('General ops agent - discretionary spend') is Active with unrestrictedMerchants = true and merchantAllowlistSize = 0, a 10 USDC total cap and a 2 USDC per-tx cap. It has made zero payments in 30 days, so there is no observed merchant behaviour to justify the open allowlist. Immediate loss is bounded by the 0.3 USDC funded, but the authorisation permits payment to any address up to the cap once funded.

findings.title: Two identical 0.49 USDC charges 7 seconds apart, both at 98% of per-tx cap
findings.detail: Intent 0x4e0866 (cloud infra autopay) made both of its payments to merchant 0x1111... at 08:09:41Z and 08:09:48Z, each 0.49 USDC = 98% of the 0.5 USDC per-tx cap. This pattern is consistent with either (a) a single ~0.98 USDC obligation split into two transactions to stay under the per-tx cap, or (b) a duplicate/retry charge. Either way the per-tx cap of 0.5 is mis-sized against the real invoice size, and the intent burned 49% of its 2 USDC total cap in one day on a purportedly weekly autopay.

findings.title: Idle capital sitting on a revoked intent
findings.detail: 0xe88b02 was revoked ('Trial ended, tool not adopted') after a single 0.2 USDC payment, leaving 0.8 USDC of the 1 USDC funded unspent and unrecoverable until withdrawRemainder is called. Small in absolute terms but it is 100% of the reported idle capital and there is no reason to leave it stranded.

findings.title: Controls are otherwise clean on the spending intents
findings.detail: All 4 payments carry receipts, every intent that actually transacted has a single-merchant allowlist, and no payment exceeded its per-tx cap. Spend is concentrated in one merchant (0x1111..., 0.98 USDC of 1.28 total), which is expected for infra autopay.

actions.rationale: Highest-risk configuration in the set: open allowlist, 10 USDC cap, 2 USDC per-tx cap, and zero payments in 30 days to justify it. Pin it to the specific merchants ops actually needs before any further funding; if none can be named, revoke instead since it has never been used.

50 USDC authorised against 0.1 USDC spent (0.2%) and a single payment. Cutting the cap to roughly 5 USDC still leaves ~50x headroom over observed spend while removing 45 USDC of standing authorisation - the single largest exposure reduction available.
Intent is Revoked with the trial explicitly abandoned; 0.8 USDC of funded value is stranded and serves no purpose on-chain.

Both payments hit 98% of the 0.5 USDC per-tx cap seconds apart, which indicates the agent is splitting a single ~0.98 USDC invoice to fit under the cap - splitting defeats the control. Confirm the two charges are not duplicates first; if legitimate, size per-tx cap to the real invoice (~1.0-1.2 USDC) so each payment is one auditable transaction, and review the 2 USDC total cap since 49% was consumed on day one.

dataGaps: All 4 payments occurred within a 64-second span on 2026-09-13 despite a 30-day window, so there is no spend history to establish a baseline or trend - burn-rate and cap-sizing conclusions rest on a single day.
No receipt contents or invoice references, so the two 0.49 USDC charges to 0x1111... cannot be confirmed as a split invoice versus a duplicate charge.
No merchant identity or labelling for 0x1111..., 0x2222..., 0x3333..., so merchant-level appropriateness cannot be assessed.
No declared billing cadence or expected invoice amount for the 'weekly' cloud infra autopay, so the correct per-tx and total cap cannot be computed precisely.
No treasury balance or top-up policy, so it is unclear whether low fundedUsdc values (0.3-1.2 USDC) are deliberate drip-funding or an oversight relative to the much larger caps.
